Concepts of Community Health Nursing

Community health nursing concepts — community, health, primary health care, levels of prevention and the nurse’s role.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define community and community health
  • Describe primary health care and its elements
  • Explain the levels of prevention
  • List the roles of the community health nurse

In simple words

Community health nursing is the care of groups of people in the place where they live, work and learn, not only of individuals in a hospital. The aim is to prevent disease, promote health and bring care to the doorstep.

Basic concepts

Term Meaning
Community A group of people living in a defined area with shared interests
Community health The health of all people living in that community
Public health Science and art of preventing disease and prolonging life
Primary health care Essential care based on practical, scientific and acceptable methods
Health for all Universal, equitable health coverage (Alma-Ata 1978)

Primary health care — five elements

  1. Health education
  2. Locally endemic disease prevention and control
  3. Promotion of safe food supply and proper nutrition
  4. Adequate safe water and basic sanitation
  5. Maternal and child health and family welfare (plus immunisation, treatment of common illness, essential drugs)

Levels of prevention

Level What is done
Health promotion Nutrition education, immunisation, health education
Specific protection Vaccines, safe water, sanitation, food hygiene
Early diagnosis and treatment Screening, case finding, prompt treatment
Disability limitation Rehabilitation, physiotherapy, aids
Rehabilitation Return the person to a useful life

Nurse’s roles in the community

  • Direct caregiver to individuals and families
  • Teacher of health and health education
  • Planner of health programmes and camps
  • Supervisor of ASHA, Anganwadi workers and health volunteers
  • Epidemiologist — case finding, contact tracing, reporting
  • Advocate for the vulnerable and for resources
  • Team member in national health programmes

🔴 Primary health care is essential care

PHC is not second-class care. It is scientifically sound, socially acceptable, universally accessible care provided close to where people live and work, at a cost the community can afford.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Community = people living in a defined area with shared interests.
  2. Alma-Ata Declaration 1978 defines health for all through primary health care.
  3. Five elements of PHC: education, vaccination, nutrition, safe water, maternal and child health.
  4. Levels of prevention: promotion, protection, early diagnosis, disability limitation, rehabilitation.
  5. The nurse supervises ASHA workers and coordinates programmes.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Public health is the science and art of preventing disease.
  2. Community health nursing emphasises populations over individuals.
  3. The nurse is caregiver, teacher, leader, planner and advocate.
  4. Photogrammetric and epidemiologic surveillance starts in the community.
  5. Referral links primary, secondary and tertiary levels of care.

📌 Memory trick

PHC five elements: E-V-N-W-M — Education, Vaccination, Nutrition, Water, Maternal and child health.

60-second revision

  • Community health nursing = care of populations in their own setting.
  • Community, health, public health and primary health care definitions.
  • PHC from Alma-Ata 1978: essential, accessible, affordable care.
  • Five levels of prevention.
  • Nurse’s roles: caregiver, teacher, supervisor, epidemiologist, advocate.

Test yourself

The Alma-Ata Declaration was made in:

Answer: B. The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 called for Health for All through primary health care.

Which is a level of prevention?

Answer: A. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment is a recognised level of prevention between specific protection and disability limitation.

Primary health care means:

Answer: B. Primary health care is essential, scientifically sound and affordable care provided close to the community.

The community health nurse supervises:

Answer: B. The nurse guides, trains and supervises frontline workers such as ASHA and Anganwadi workers.

Which is the first element of primary health care?

Answer: A. Health education is the first element of primary health care as it enables people to act for their own health.
